subject: physics
question_text: What is potential energy? Derive an expression for the gravitational potential energy.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 6 SHORT ANSWER. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed, so appearances[] stays empty. The TSBIE Basic Learning Material has no SAQ section for this unit, so the Fastrack is the only source for it. AI physics check 2026-08-24: formulas, signs, numbers and claims verified against NCERT Class-11 conventions; corrections applied to explanation text (why / common_mistakes / memory_tip), marked answer lines unchanged unless factually wrong.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: What it is
lines: The energy possessed by a body by
virtue of its position is called
steps.margin_note: The words that earn it are "by virtue of its position". Kinetic energy is the one about motion.
steps.why: Potential energy is stored by WHERE something is, not by how fast it moves — which is why lifting a book and holding it still gives it energy.
common_mistakes: Defining it as the energy of a moving body, which is kinetic energy.

recall.must_convey: That potential energy is the energy a body has because of its position.

steps.memory_tip: Potential goes with POSITION, kinetic with MOTION. One word separates the two definitions.

steps.label: The body raised
steps.margin_note: A box lifted through h, with F up and mg down. It takes fifteen seconds and makes the next two steps obvious.
steps.why: The figure shows the two forces pointing opposite ways and the distance moved, which is everything the derivation uses.
common_mistakes: Drawing the body but not the two force arrows, so the θ = 0 claim has nothing to stand on.

recall.must_convey: That a figure of the body raised through height h is drawn, with F up and mg down.
accept: draw the body lifted through h
figure with F up and mg down
body ni h varaku ethina figure
reject: work done equals m g h

steps.memory_tip: Four things on the figure: the box, F pointing up, mg pointing down, and the height h.

steps.label: The lifting force
lines: Let a body of mass m be raised slowly
through a height h. The applied force

lines.text: F = mg,  acting along the motion

steps.margin_note: Say "slowly". That is what lets you write F = mg instead of F > mg.
steps.why: Raised slowly, the body gains no kinetic energy, so every joule the applied force supplies is stored as potential energy and none is wasted on speed.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the word "slowly", which leaves F = mg unjustified.

recall.must_convey: That the body is raised slowly so the applied force equals mg.
accept: slowly ga ethithe F equals mg

steps.memory_tip: Slowly means zero acceleration, and zero acceleration means F = mg exactly.

steps.label: The work done
lines: The force and the displacement are in
the same direction, so θ = 0° and

lines.text: W = F s cos 0° = F s

steps.margin_note: Two lines: the general formula, then the substitution. Do not jump straight to mgh.
steps.why: This is the same W = F s cos θ as every other work question. Nothing special happens because the force is gravity.
common_mistakes: Writing W = mgh with no formula above it.
Calling mgh the work done by gravity. The +mgh here is the work done by the applied lifting force; gravity does −mgh during the lift.

recall.must_convey: That the work done is F s = mgh, with θ = 0.
accept: theta is zero so W is F s
reject: this work is stored as potential energy

steps.memory_tip: cos 0° = 1, so W = F s cos θ becomes plain F × s. Then F = mg and s = h give mgh.

steps.label: The result
lines: This work is stored in the body as
steps.margin_note: The last mark is for saying the work is STORED. Do not stop at the work done.
steps.why: The work does not vanish. It comes back the moment the body is released, as kinetic energy — which is what the next question proves.
common_mistakes: Ending at W = mgh without ever calling it potential energy.

recall.must_convey: That the work is stored as gravitational potential energy, U = mgh.
accept: this work is stored as potential energy
reject: theta is zero so W is F s

steps.memory_tip: Check it with a number: 1 kg raised 1 m stores about 10 J, since mgh is force × distance.

insider_note: One mark each: the definition, F = mg, W = mgh, then U = mgh. Naming the work as STORED energy is the line most students leave out.
